newsitem.title: USA: Court backs Calif. in Golden Eagle Insurance case.
newsitem.headline: Court backs Calif. in Golden Eagle Insurance case.

text.p: A San Francisco Superior Court judge has backed California Department of Insurance in a dispute with Golden Eagle Insurance Co over the company's reserves, state insurance officials said Monday.
Judge William Cahill said the Department of Insurance acted properly in issuing an order to Golden Eagle Insurance to increase its reserves.
The judge also ruled that the state's insurance department afforded Golden Eagle due process before it issued and filed its report showing the firm has a reserve deficiency of $138.5 million.
California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush has given Golden Eagle Insurance until Oct 7 to submit a plan to correct the reserve deficiency by Nov 15.
"My directive to the Department staff was to ask Golden Eagle to submit a plan to correct the reserve shortage," Quackenbush said in a statement.

"Sadly, rather than work with us to achieve an equitable resolution to this problem, Golden Eagle decided to launch a public barrage against this office and take the Department of Insurance to court," he said.
Golden Eagle Insurance, which is privately held, is the state's third largest workers compensation insurer.
A spokesman for the company was not immediately available to comment. But earlier this month, the company said in a statement that it believed its reserves were adequate.
